rule: Scope is everything the tool scans, except paths with a segment named exactly `test`, `tests`, `spec`, `examples` or `docs`. | C4 Unresolved references are preserved. A call the tool cannot resolve is still emitted as a low guess (`recv.m`, `.m`, a bare name). It is never dropped and never promoted to a resolved ID.
source: KNOWN_GAP: packages that fail to type-check are not graphed (reported in coverage)
notes: Package broken has two type errors (a string assigned to an int; the undefined function missing). SPEC's scope covers every scanned file and its ID/tier rules decide each call independently of type errors: fmt.Println (medium), helper defined in the scan (high), and missing, a bare name not found in the scan (low, C4: never dropped). main's call to broken.Run resolves to the scanned definition (high). Per the gap, a coverage note alone does not produce these edges; SPEC requires them.
